title: George Jones and cabaret work for Harris Stilley
summary: George Jones got jobs in the Basin and Bienville cabarets; Gallaud played Bourbon Street cabarets for Harris Stilley with Buddy Bertrand and a violinist.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: Oh, yeah, that's George Jones. He used to get all the jobs around there and play. That's the time, that's the old time. He used to play guitar and bass too and sing, you know. He was in a, during the time, Cornelius, Washington, and them used to have a, all them cabarets around, uh, uh, Basin and, uh, in Bienville. Basin and Bienville by Louis White there. And, uh, he used to play in that place there. And I used to play for Harris Stilley too at Countdown in Bourbon. And also at Corndown in St. Louis for Harris Stilley. He died. What was his last name?
Mm-hmm. Little bit of short-filling. Cabaret.
Cabaret. When Buddy Bertrand was with it, eh? And, uh, let's see who was there with me then. Uh, we had, uh, clean drum.
I've heard of a Buddy Bertrand, uh, Jolly Roll, um,

Yeah, he was, he played piano too. He played piano too. He died some time ago. He used to be around 25 all the time. He used to play piano around there sometime. And when we used to get off, I used to go around there. Well, I used to have a violin player there, Willie Dan's boy. Oh, yeah. Playing violin from Baton Rouge. He's in Baton Rouge. He was sick some time ago. I tried to find him. But he used to come here. Well, he's in Baton Rouge. You think he's still up there then? Yeah, he's still living. He still was at the hospital down here. I don't know if he's living yet. I never heard nothing. We tried to find him last year.
We were trying, we didn't never, didn't find anybody.

Well, I'm gonna try to get in touch with him, you see, because he used to play with me and he used to get all that job and work around. I'd like to talk to him sometime. All around Bourbon Street, that was our wait quarters. All around that we used to play.
